items.title: Codebase Maintenance in Antigravity
items.takeaway: Use a bounded maintenance task to evaluate edits, tool use, and verification together.
items.body_notes: Antigravity's launch demonstration shows Hydrogen maintaining a codebase. It is a platform-produced example, not an independently reproduced engineering benchmark.

items.title: Sixteen Parallel Canvas Apps
items.takeaway: Split a build into independent modules and keep planning, implementation, and QA roles explicit.
items.body_notes: An Antigravity CLI creator at Google DeepMind describes Carbon coordinating, verifying, and integrating while Hydrogen builds 16 zero-dependency canvas mini-apps. This is a mixed-model workflow, so its outcome should not be attributed to Hydrogen alone.

items.title: Crimson Moth with a Mixed-Model Swarm
items.takeaway: Use separate orchestration and implementation roles for an interactive creative-code project.
items.body_notes: The creator says Carbon orchestrated an Antigravity swarm while Hydrogen workers built the crimson-moth artwork. The reported 45-minute duration includes that multi-model workflow and was not independently timed.

items.title: 3D Medic Inspection and Repair
items.takeaway: Explore an agent that inspects a 3D file, finds errors, and proposes repairs before export.
items.body_notes: Google AI's 3D Medic demonstration uses a Managed Agent app built in AI Studio. It shows a file-repair workflow rather than evidence that arbitrary 3D assets will be repaired correctly.

items.title: A Sailboat Scene Built in Devin
items.takeaway: Evaluate a model inside the actual coding-agent environment you intend to use.
items.body_notes: The source presents a sailboat scene attributed to Hydrogen running inside Devin. The short post does not disclose a complete prompt, iteration history, or reproducible setup.

items.title: Lingo City Language Practice
items.takeaway: Combine flashcards with an interactive street scene for contextual language practice.
items.body_notes: Tulsee Doshi shares a Google example that streams custom 2D and 3D flashcards and lets a learner practice shopkeeper conversations in a virtual city. This is a provider demonstration, not an independent learning-outcome study.

items.title: Romeo and Juliet as a 3D Paper Theatre
items.takeaway: Turn a specific lesson into an interactive scene with a clear learning objective.
items.body_notes: The creator built a 3D paper-theatre lesson about the balcony scene in Romeo and Juliet for GCSE English Literature. The source demonstrates the interface, but does not measure learning outcomes.

items.title: Design Image to Reading Website
items.takeaway: Use a reference design to evaluate visual understanding and working frontend implementation.
items.body_notes: The creator says Hydrogen turned a design image into a functioning reading-management website in 5 minutes 27 seconds. The duration and completeness are source claims; no independent functional test accompanies this collection.

items.title: A Koi Garden Built in Twenty Modules
items.takeaway: Build a larger scene in small modules instead of expecting a complete result from one prompt.
items.body_notes: The creator reports 20 prompts for 20 modules inside the Gemini app, with each taking 90–270 seconds. The author disclosed early access, and the example is explicitly iterative rather than a one-shot result.

items.title: A Proton-Fusion Learning Game
items.takeaway: Prototype an interactive explanation of a scientific process, then check the underlying science.
items.body_notes: The creator's game moves through the proton–proton chain inside a young star. The reported one prompt, 78-second runtime, and roughly $0.19 cost are source claims, not independently reproduced results.

items.title: An Animated Landscape in Google Sheets
items.takeaway: Use an unconventional spreadsheet animation to inspect generated code and cell-level updates.
items.body_notes: Google demonstrates coastal trains, clouds, and autumn leaves painted across spreadsheet cells with code written in Antigravity. It is an official creative demonstration, not a spreadsheet-performance benchmark.

items.title: Folio Interactive Data Website
items.takeaway: Combine a landing-page layout with interactive data visualizations in a small web prototype.
items.body_notes: A Google DeepMind staff member presents a Folio-style website and interactive animation built using Google AI Studio. The post does not provide the complete generation prompt or an independent functional test.

items.title: Visual Answers to Multi-Part Search Questions
items.takeaway: Compare answer layout and cited links when testing a nuanced, multi-constraint search request.
items.body_notes: Google's Search example combines intent understanding, visual layouts, comparison tables, and query fan-out. These are provider-described product behaviors; the demonstration does not establish ranking or traffic effects for publishers.

items.title: Interactive Financial Forecasting in Sheets
items.takeaway: Prototype a financial model with visible assumptions and inspect the generated formulas and charts.
items.body_notes: Chandu Thota presents a Google Sheets forecasting demonstration. The source's claim of over 30% faster canvas generation is a provider claim, not a controlled timing measurement performed for this repository.

items.title: An Interactive Dining Room
items.takeaway: Check object interactions, lighting, and state changes rather than judging a scene from a still image.
items.body_notes: The creator shows a dining room with interactive lights, lamps, a fridge, and items inside it. The reported 30-minute build time is not independently verified.

items.title: A Volume Slider with a Miniature World
items.takeaway: Use one familiar control to test both interaction design and animated scene detail.
items.body_notes: The source shows a volume slider that animates a tiny Japanese-style world. The creator reports $0.19 in cost, but does not provide a bill or full generation workflow.

items.title: A Japanese House in Three.js
items.takeaway: Separate code generation from rendering time when evaluating a detailed 3D walkthrough.
items.body_notes: The creator attributes this house and garden to Hydrogen in Three.js without agents. The post's subscription-usage and under-two-hour claims are specific to that author's setup and are not general pricing or latency guarantees.

items.title: A Pelican Riding a Bicycle in 3D
items.takeaway: Use a moving character to inspect coordination, motion, and scene consistency.
items.body_notes: The creator presents a 3D animated pelican riding a bicycle and labels the model Hydrogen at XHigh. The post is an output demonstration, not a complete reproducible prompt or physics validation.

items.title: A Plan-First Planet Simulator
items.takeaway: Give the coding model a concrete plan before asking it to edit a complex scene.
items.body_notes: The early-access creator shows a planet simulator and reports better editing results after supplying more detailed plans. The source credits ForwardEditor for the idea and describes an iterative workflow.

items.title: A Harbor Island with Antigravity Swarm
items.takeaway: Use a small navigable environment to inspect multi-agent scene-building behavior.
items.body_notes: The creator disclosed early access and shows a harbor island built with Hydrogen inside Antigravity's Swarm feature. The public post does not specify the entire orchestration or prompt history.

items.title: An Eiffel Tower Floating Island
items.takeaway: Evaluate composition, camera motion, and model-generated code on a compact landmark scene.
items.body_notes: The source shows an Eiffel Tower miniature island and attributes it to Hydrogen XHigh. The six-minute build-and-recording claim is the author's report, not an independent timing test.

items.title: A Flyable Futuristic City
items.takeaway: Test follow-up edits on a procedural world rather than assuming the first output is final.
items.body_notes: The early-access creator used Hydrogen High in Antigravity and reports one follow-up to produce a Three.js city with procedural towers, rain, and flying traffic. The recording shows generated code running, not native video generation.

items.title: A Seaplane from Sunrise to Night
items.takeaway: Inspect environmental controls and lighting transitions in an interactive 3D scene.
items.body_notes: LuminaBench's original demonstration shows a seaplane and changing time of day, later reshared by Google. The post predates the recorded public-release boundary; its access route and model invocation were not independently verified.

items.title: Neon Stickman Animation: Hydrogen and Opus
items.takeaway: Compare the finished animation alongside reported time and cost, without assuming identical harnesses.
items.body_notes: The author presents Hydrogen and Opus 5.5 outputs and reports $1.02 versus $7.43 and 10m 22s versus 34m. The collection has not verified billing, prompts, iteration counts, or comparable runtime settings.

items.title: Robotics Tasks and Self-Reported Mistakes
items.takeaway: Include task completion and recognition of small mistakes in a robotics evaluation.
items.body_notes: Artificial Analysis shows pouring and block-tidying tasks and says Hydrogen noticed a small spill and an unclosed lid. The video and AA-Robotics v0.1 ranking come from the evaluator; they are not independent replication here.

items.title: A Natural-Language Laboratory Workcell
items.takeaway: Evaluate tool execution and failure handling separately from benchmark headline scores.
items.body_notes: The source shows a laboratory workcell driven by a natural-language request and reports results on four lab-related benchmarks. Hydrogen's reported RareBench score is lower than Opus 5.5's, while the other three are higher; this is a benchmark-owner demonstration, not medical validation.

items.title: Iceberg and Tugboat: Hydrogen and Carbon
items.takeaway: Record reasoning level and harness restrictions when comparing a long 3D build.
items.body_notes: The creator reports both models running on High through OpenRouter, with Hydrogen at $4.27 and 1h 23m 40s versus Carbon at $8.83 and 2h 39m 10s. These are uncontrolled, source-reported results, not universal price or speed ratios.

items.title: A Jelly Koi Pond: Hydrogen and Sonnet
items.takeaway: Inspect a concrete scene before turning a benchmark ranking into a model choice.
items.body_notes: The author compares Hydrogen and Sonnet 5.5 on a 3D koi-pond task. The source asks viewers to judge the outputs but does not establish matched settings or an objective quality score.

items.title: A Shared-Prompt Creative-Code Collection
items.takeaway: Use a set of varied visual tasks to avoid overgeneralizing from one attractive output.
items.body_notes: The creator reports giving Hydrogen, Carbon, and Argon the same prompts and places comparisons in replies. The root post's media shows low-poly animals, a neon street, and a watercolor-style container; it is not a complete controlled benchmark.

items.title: Megamind Voxels: A Cost and Quality Counterexample
items.takeaway: Keep failure cases when assessing whether a model is consistently cheaper or visually stronger.
items.body_notes: The source says Hydrogen produced a less coherent Titan figure while costing $36.07, versus $8.64 for Sonnet 5.5. The post includes a commercial promotion, and the costs and quality judgment are the publisher's claims.

items.title: A Juggling Lion Across Four Seasons
items.takeaway: Check the requested motion, not only the visual polish of the surrounding interface.
items.body_notes: The author reports that Carbon handled crossing juggling arcs while Hydrogen left balls floating, despite cleaner season transitions and clipping. This same-task SVG comparison exposes a specific motion failure rather than an overall model ranking.

items.title: Three-Model Stickman Fight: A Slower, Costlier Result
items.takeaway: Retain counterexamples when comparing a model's advertised efficiency with real task reports.
items.body_notes: The creator compares Hydrogen, Carbon, and Argon and reports Hydrogen taking longer and costing more than Carbon in this test. Settings, billing, and iteration counts have not been independently verified.

items.title: A Farm Bicycle Scene: Hydrogen and Flash
items.takeaway: Compare motion and scene quality alongside the creator's reported completion time.
items.body_notes: The source compares Hydrogen with Gemini 3.8 Flash on a farm bicycle scene and reports 56 seconds versus more than six minutes. This is a single creator test, not a general speed benchmark.

items.title: A Girl and Cat on Tandem Bikes
items.takeaway: Compare prompt fidelity and extra detailing while keeping different coding harnesses visible.
items.body_notes: The creator used the same stated SVG task but ran Opus 5.5 in Claude Code and Hydrogen in Cursor. Reported time and cost differ substantially, but different harnesses and undisclosed iterations prevent a controlled model-only comparison.

items.title: Four Models Build a Three.js Mario Game
items.takeaway: Record unequal reasoning settings before interpreting a same-prompt game comparison.
items.body_notes: The source compares Gemini 3.8 Flash, Argon, and Carbon on High with Hydrogen on XHigh, using pure Three.js without external 3D models or textures. It shows four outputs, not a matched-reasoning benchmark.

items.title: Three Gemini Models Draw a Controller
items.takeaway: Look for task-specific regressions and improvements rather than assuming a family hierarchy.
items.body_notes: The creator compares controller SVG outputs from Carbon, Argon, and Hydrogen and reports rerunning the test. The reported durations and costs are source claims and do not establish a general ordering of model quality.

items.title: Vision Answers Differ Between App and Studio
items.takeaway: Test the same image in your intended product surface before relying on a vision result.
items.body_notes: The source shows conflicting food-identification responses attributed to Hydrogen in the Gemini app and AI Studio. The comparison does not independently verify identical routing, settings, or full conversation context.

items.title: A Rocket Launch Scene: Hydrogen and Flash
items.takeaway: Compare the actual launch animation as well as the reported build duration.
items.body_notes: The creator presents Hydrogen and Gemini 3.8 Flash outputs and reports under one minute versus roughly three minutes. The visual comparison is one task with no independently controlled runtime setup.

items.title: Four SVG Animation Tasks
items.takeaway: Use several interaction and animation motifs to inspect consistency across tasks.
items.body_notes: The source pairs Hydrogen and Carbon outputs for transfers, day/night changes, unboxing, and a chameleon. Its short root text does not disclose full prompts, timing evidence, or an objective scoring method.

items.title: Three Models Animate a Savannah Horse
items.takeaway: Inspect motion and visual detail directly before accepting broad cost or quality claims.
items.body_notes: The creator presents Hydrogen, Carbon, and Argon on a savannah-horse scene. Claims of faster speed, lower cost, and high quality remain the source's assessment, not a controlled comparison reproduced here.

items.title: Turning Space References into an HTML Scene
items.takeaway: Use a small reference set to test whether a generated scene carries a recognizable visual style.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Hydrogen with a space visualization. The source shows planetary images given to the model and a resulting HTML scene with a ringed planet.

items.title: A Formula One Prototype in Gemini Canvas
items.takeaway: Give a vehicle viewer several camera presets to inspect a generated model from different angles.
items.body_notes: The creator attributes a Formula One-style car viewer to their first Hydrogen attempt in Gemini Canvas. The recording shows several camera presets and suspension views.

items.title: Hydrogen API and Carbon Antigravity Outputs
items.takeaway: Record the harness for each run when comparing visuals from the same prompt.
items.body_notes: The creator runs Hydrogen directly through the API and Carbon through Antigravity, then shows the two outputs side by side. The reported 4 minutes 47 seconds applies to the Hydrogen run in that setup.

items.title: Shadow Detail in a Hydrogen–Astra Comparison
items.takeaway: Judge small rendering details alongside the cost and elapsed time of both runs.
items.body_notes: The creator preferred the Hydrogen rendering because it included a shadow and reports it completed faster in their setup.

items.title: A Procedural 3D Motion Comparison
items.takeaway: Record generation time while comparing continuity and composition in a procedural motion scene.
items.body_notes: The creator shows a striped 3D form attributed to Hydrogen High and reports building it in under five minutes. They compare the result with runs from more expensive models in their own test.

items.title: An 89-Minute PokéBench Vision Run
items.takeaway: Record turns and API failures alongside task completion in a long-running vision-agent test.
items.body_notes: The source reports a pre-announcement Vertex run at High in which Hydrogen cleared Brock in 365 turns across 89 minutes, with zero failed API calls. The result is specific to the recorded harness.

items.title: Hydrogen and DeepSeek Build the Same 3D Scene
items.takeaway: Record time and API charges separately while comparing the visual outputs.
items.body_notes: AIHubMix compares Hydrogen and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on one 3D scene prompt using each model’s highest available reasoning. The provider reports three minutes at $1.30 for Hydrogen and 100 minutes at $0.90 for DeepSeek.

items.title: A BMW Side Profile in SVG
items.takeaway: Use an SVG vehicle side view to inspect proportions, silhouettes, and small details.
items.body_notes: The author shows a BMW M4 CS side-view SVG attributed to Hydrogen High in the Gemini app and reports a generation time under 30 seconds.

items.title: An Astronomer’s Floating Island
items.takeaway: Give a small scene a strong visual theme and check whether its objects and lighting reinforce it.
items.body_notes: The creator credits a Hydrogen checkpoint on Arena for an astronomer’s floating-island scene and reports four minutes for the generation. The attribution describes that Arena run.

items.title: Image Reference to a Walkable 3D Landscape
items.takeaway: Check whether an image-based scene supports both visual fidelity and movement.
items.body_notes: The creator shows a playable 3D landscape attributed to Hydrogen in the Gemini app and describes GLSL reflections, procedural geometry and swimming physics.

items.title: A Miniature Diorama from 3D Blocks
items.takeaway: Ask for a block-built miniature and inspect whether the shapes read as a coherent scene.
items.body_notes: The creator shares a recorded 3D miniature blocks diorama and attributes it to Hydrogen. Build time and exact setup are unspecified.

items.title: An Interactive Cherry Blossom Tree
items.takeaway: Use one animated object and a few controls to explore real-time changes in a miniature scene.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Hydrogen for the cherry blossom tree interface in their screenshot. The visible controls include scene settings, while implementation details are unspecified.

items.title: Agent Arena Time and Cost per Task
items.takeaway: Check per-task latency, cost and output tokens alongside aggregate success.
items.body_notes: Agent Arena reports a median 5.3 minutes and $1.60 per task for Hydrogen High across its evaluation. It also reports higher output-token use than Carbon and Argon.

items.title: Visual Document and Terminal Benchmarks
items.takeaway: Check document and terminal results separately when choosing a reasoning budget.
items.body_notes: Artificial Analysis reports strong visual-document results and uneven terminal gains. Extra reasoning improved its science-terminal score while its general Terminal-Bench score stayed at 54%.

items.title: Vals Index and Tax Agent Results
items.takeaway: Inspect a specialist task score alongside the aggregate evaluation.
items.body_notes: Vals AI reports 68.5% on its index and first place on Tax Agent at the time of testing.

items.title: Hydrogen at Default Effort in CursorBench
items.takeaway: Use a default-effort score as a starting point for testing your own repository.
items.body_notes: Cursor reports 54.3% for Hydrogen at default effort versus 39.6% for Gemini 3.8 Flash on its own benchmark.

items.title: Four Models Animate an Archer Battle
items.takeaway: Compare how clearly each animation communicates the combatants’ actions.
items.body_notes: The creator shares an archer battle comparison featuring Hydrogen, Fable 5.2, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Carbon. The clip presents the runs side by side.

items.title: A Minecraft-Style Prototype in Fifteen Minutes
items.takeaway: Use a voxel sandbox to test whether generated systems such as mining and inventory fit together.
items.body_notes: The creator reports building a Minecraft-style prototype with Hydrogen Extra High in 15 minutes. They list placement, mining, and inventory, which the recording does not demonstrate comprehensively.

items.title: A Hydrogen Tool-Use Workflow in n8n
items.takeaway: Assign tool-use loops to Hydrogen inside n8n and keep planning as a separate step.
items.body_notes: n8n documents Hydrogen support and suggests using Carbon or Argon to plan and Hydrogen to execute. The post links the integration setup.

items.title: Box Agent on Complex Enterprise Documents
items.takeaway: Check accuracy, runtime and token use on a realistic document workload.
items.body_notes: Box reports a five-point accuracy gain over Gemini 3.8 Flash, less than half the runtime and about 12% fewer tokens on a typical task in its early-access evaluation.

items.title: Hydrogen on Devin FrontierCode
items.takeaway: Compare candidate patches for mergeability and record the agent harness.
items.body_notes: Cognition reports 38.2% on FrontierCode 2.0. Its test setup for Hydrogen differs from the Devin CLI setup used for comparison models.

items.title: Refraction in a Small Interactive Animation
items.takeaway: Use quick previews to refine an optical effect before adding more scene complexity.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Hydrogen for an animated mini-experience in the Small Delights series and points readers to the refraction effect. The source describes an iterative creative workflow.

items.title: A River That Flows Upward
items.takeaway: Test a small scene with an unusual direction of motion and inspect the effect visually.
items.body_notes: The author reports building a reverse-flowing river with Hydrogen on the web and shares the recorded output. The time and subscription allowance usage are source observations.

items.title: Web Search Despite an Explicit Constraint
items.takeaway: Verify whether tools stayed unused when a workflow requires an answer without browsing.
items.body_notes: The author reports that Hydrogen performed a web search despite an instruction to avoid searching and tool calls. The post shows an example rather than measuring how often it occurs.

items.title: Tracking Quota Use During an Antigravity Swarm
items.takeaway: Record token volume and quota consumed when testing a multi-agent run.
items.body_notes: The creator reports using 17 million tokens and 21% of a five-hour allowance while using Swarm on their plan. The numbers are specific to that session.

items.title: Tool Calls in Professional Work Benchmarks
items.takeaway: Inspect how an agent gathers context before acting on professional tasks.
items.body_notes: Mercor reports 78.0% Pass@1 on APEX-Agents and an average of 93 tool calls per task. Its report covers law, consulting and banking.

items.title: A 3D Portrait from Hydrogen
items.takeaway: Use a portrait as a compact test of whether a 3D representation conveys a recognizable subject.
items.body_notes: The author credits Hydrogen for a 3D portrait of the person addressed in the post and shares the result as an image. The source provides limited setup details.

items.title: Four Models Animate a Mage and Dragon
items.takeaway: Compare staging, readable actions, and effects across generated versions of the same fantasy scene.
items.body_notes: The comparison clip shows Hydrogen and three Claude models on a mage-versus-dragon scene. The creator preferred the Claude output in this example.

items.title: Authentication Routing in a Multi-Agent Setup
items.takeaway: Check which client actually authenticates when an agent delegates work to another provider.
items.body_notes: The author reports asking Claude to use Hydrogen through Antigravity CLI, then seeing Claude Code attempt authentication directly and Antigravity access get suspended. The screenshot shows a suspension notice; the author attributes the incident to the client route.

items.title: A Goal Mode Run in Antigravity
items.takeaway: Track the plan, code changes and test results in a long-running coding session.
items.body_notes: The author reports a 105-minute Goal Mode session in Hydrogen Extra covering planning, implementation and tests. The test results are author-reported.

items.title: MazeBench Exposes Low Success Rates
items.takeaway: Use maze tasks to check spatial reasoning before relying on it.
items.body_notes: The posted MazeBench comparison reports 1% for Hydrogen, 4% for Sonnet 5.5 and 8% for GPT-6.1 Terra under its test setup.

items.title: Three Gemini Models Build Sailing Ship Scenes
items.takeaway: Compare motion and environmental detail in a themed Three.js scene.
items.body_notes: The creator shares sailing ship outputs from Hydrogen, Argon and Carbon. They prefer Carbon’s detail and say Hydrogen came close to Argon in their test.

items.title: Carbon and Hydrogen in Antigravity Orchestrator
items.takeaway: Use a planner to recover when a faster implementation model gets stuck.
items.body_notes: Google describes Carbon planning and recovering while Hydrogen edits and tests. Google reports near-Carbon Terminal-Bench 4.0 success with lower quota use and shorter runs.

items.title: Charts and a Report from Workspace Data
items.takeaway: Check whether a follow-up turn fixes missing analysis, charts, or report output.
items.body_notes: The creator used Hydrogen in a Google Workspace for Education Fundamentals demo to analyze data, generate a chart, and produce a report file. They report needing two exchanges.

items.title: When Jersey-Number Recognition Exhausts the Budget
items.takeaway: Set an effort limit and a fallback when reading a small image detail.
items.body_notes: The evaluator reports that Hydrogen XHigh used 131,069 thinking tokens and returned no jersey number after 9 minutes and 55 seconds.

items.title: Comparing ClutterBench Performance Across Model Families
items.takeaway: Use a clutter-focused benchmark to check whether a model family’s general strengths carry over to that task.
items.body_notes: The author shares ClutterBench results where Hydrogen leads the Gemini entries shown but trails OpenAI models in the comparison.

items.title: A News Brief into a Narrated Clip
items.takeaway: Turn a researched news brief into a short narration-led video and check the surfaced facts.
items.body_notes: The creator records Hydrogen in the Gemini mobile app searching recent news and drafting an outline before requesting the video. The clip shows ten-second playback in the app. Generation time and narration are reported by the creator, and the rendering backend is unspecified.

items.title: A Minecraft Anatomical Cutaway Bust
items.takeaway: Check whether a generated cutaway includes the requested internal structures.
items.body_notes: The creator gave Hydrogen and Argon the same one-shot task to build a Minecraft-style anatomical bust. They report identifying a skull, ribs and spine in Hydrogen’s result.

items.title: Three Models Render the Same Prop
items.takeaway: Track tokens and quality independently when a cheaper model may use more tokens in a single test.
items.body_notes: The comparison shows Hydrogen, Carbon, and Fable 5.2 rendering the same rifle-shaped prop. The creator reports 3.69 million tokens and $1.62 for Hydrogen, compared with 398,000 tokens and $0.77 for Carbon.

items.title: Induction Benchmark and Token Consumption
items.takeaway: Track total billed input and output alongside reasoning scores on difficult tasks.
items.body_notes: The evaluator reports that Hydrogen placed fourth in their 100-problem induction benchmark, near Opus 5.5. They report 55 million output tokens and 307 million billed input tokens and leave the accounting mechanism unresolved.

items.title: Spreadsheet Pixel Art Across Gemini Modes
items.takeaway: Use the same Google Sheets drawing task to compare several model choices.
items.body_notes: The creator records Hydrogen drawing pixel art in Google Sheets and links separate runs with Antigravity Orchestrator, Carbon, and Argon. It is a creator demonstration without a formal scoring method.

items.title: Printing an Apartment from a Reference Image
items.takeaway: Carry an image-to-3D test through to a physical print.
items.body_notes: The author shares a reference image and a physical print of a Seinfeld apartment model they attribute to Hydrogen.

items.title: Three Models Animate a 3D Animal
items.takeaway: Inspect anatomy and motion in a shared 3D animal-modeling test.
items.body_notes: The source compares Hydrogen, GPT-6.1 Terra, and Claude Haiku 5.5 in one visual modeling task. The creator observes weaknesses in the Hydrogen output; the clip does not support a general ranking across all 3D tasks.

items.title: Hydrogen and Qwen on ts-bench
items.takeaway: Review tool-call errors alongside overall benchmark results.
items.body_notes: The source compares Hydrogen and Qwen4 Max Preview on ts-bench and comments on tool-call reliability in the reported runs. The benchmark screenshot provides the evaluation snapshot.

items.title: Vending-Bench Business Simulation
items.takeaway: Compare simulated revenue alongside the cost of operating the agent.
items.body_notes: Andon Labs reports Hydrogen placed third on Vending-Bench 2 and earned more than similarly priced models in its simulation.

items.title: A Golden Merry Ship Scene
items.takeaway: Use a familiar fictional ship to check stylized nautical scene composition.
items.body_notes: The creator attributes the Golden Merry scene to Hydrogen and shares a clip showing the ship on blue water. The post does not specify prompts, tool settings, or iteration count.

items.title: Hydrogen in OpenClaw
items.takeaway: Check model selection inside the agent framework you plan to use.
items.body_notes: OpenClaw announces Hydrogen support and includes a screenshot. The post provides no benchmark or setup transcript.

items.title: A Whale Moving Through Clouds
items.takeaway: Use a coded creature scene to check fluid motion and eye design independently.
items.body_notes: The source shows a code-built whale moving through clouds and reports a roughly two-minute run in Hydrogen. Timing and quota are the author's observations.

items.title: Four Models Build a Miniature Island
items.takeaway: Compare island designs alongside the elapsed time and pricing of each environment.
items.body_notes: The source compares four miniature-island outputs and reports 4 minutes for Hydrogen, 20 for GPT-6.1 Terra, 40 for Sol, and 60 for DeepSeek. The author's zero incremental Hydrogen charge reflects their setup.

items.title: A Webcam Air Sketch Tool
items.takeaway: Test camera-driven drawing by tracing strokes and observing how the interface follows them.
items.body_notes: The creator reports using early access to Hydrogen to build a webcam air sketch tool and shares a recorded demonstration.

items.title: Comparing Cloth Tears in Code
items.takeaway: Test stretch, tearing, and fur interaction in the same scripted animation brief.
items.body_notes: The creator compares code-generated animations from Hydrogen and Claude Fable 5.2. The post flags the latter as visually stronger but provides no matched settings or independent physics validation.

items.title: An Underwater City in Gemini Canvas
items.takeaway: Start from a small 3D scene and add explorable areas and animated wildlife over several turns.
items.body_notes: The creator iterated inside the Gemini app to build an underwater city with fish, jellyfish, coral, and navigable glass domes. The source explicitly describes multiple prompts.

items.title: A One-Pass Web Portal
items.takeaway: Use a portal layout to assess the first UI pass before testing individual flows.
items.body_notes: The author shows a portal-page screenshot built with Hydrogen in Antigravity and reports a single generation. The screenshot does not establish whether the portal's interactions work.

items.title: Fact-Checking with an Untraceable Source
items.takeaway: Require an inspectable citation before acting on a verdict about a screenshot.
items.body_notes: The author asked Hydrogen whether a screenshot of a post was accurate. They report that the model confirmed it, repeatedly opened a verification tool, and withheld the underlying source.

items.title: A Cities: Skylines-Style City Builder
items.takeaway: Prototype a city builder and inspect how its controls and simulations fit together.
items.body_notes: The creator shows a Cities: Skylines-style output they attribute to Hydrogen and reports a generation session of under 30 minutes. The clip illustrates the prototype.

items.title: Hydrogen and Sol Draw a 2D Pelican
items.takeaway: Compare turnaround and motion quality for a simple 2D animation with one shared task.
items.body_notes: The author's clip shows Hydrogen and GPT-6.1 Sol outputs on a 2D pelican cycling test. They report 28 seconds for Hydrogen and 6 minutes 51 seconds for Sol; the source does not establish matched execution settings.

items.title: A Throne Room with Blender MCP
items.takeaway: Use Blender MCP to inspect a generated scene’s composition in the editor.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Hydrogen with recreating the Iron Throne hall from Game of Thrones using Blender MCP and shares a recording of the resulting scene.

items.title: Four Models Build a Web-Swinging Game
items.takeaway: Compare traversal and controls in games built under the same single-file constraint.
items.body_notes: The source shows four Gemini models on the same 3D web-swinging challenge in a standalone HTML file with no external assets. Hydrogen used Extra High while Gemini 3.8 Flash, Argon, and Carbon used High.

items.prompt_text:
今開いている動画の内容を、初めて見る人にも分かるように要約してください。

# 出力の構成
1. **ひとことで**：この動画が何を伝えているかを1〜2文で。
2. **要点**：重要なポイントを5〜8個の箇条書きで。可能ならタイムスタンプ（例 03:12）を付ける。
3. **詳しい流れ**：話の展開を章ごとに整理。専門用語は初出時にかみ砕いて説明する。
4. **関連情報**：動画内で触れられた人物・製品・研究・出来事について、背景知識や最新の関連情報をWebから補足する。動画内の情報と外部情報ははっきり区別し、外部情報には出典URLを付ける。
5. **注意点**：動画の主張で事実と異なる・古い・議論がある部分があれば指摘する。
6. **さらに知りたい人へ**：次に読む・見るとよいリソースを3つ。

# ルール
- 日本語で、中学生にも伝わる平易な言葉で書く。
- 推測で埋めず、動画で言っていないことは「動画内では言及なし」と書く。
- 数字・固有名詞は正確に残す。

items.title: A Google Drive Handoff to Muse
items.takeaway: Hand off research through a watched Drive folder when a second agent owns the next step.
items.body_notes: The author describes using Hydrogen to gather and organize information into a Drive file, then having Muse watch Drive and take over when the file appears. The diagram documents the handoff.

items.title: A Recorder Guide in Gemini Canvas
items.takeaway: Try fast mode for a practice aid that pairs sheet music with instrument guidance.
items.body_notes: The video shows a recorder-guide Canvas app built with Hydrogen fast mode. The creator reports that the app could also be made from imported sheet music.

items.title: Project Estimates Swing with Added Scope
items.takeaway: Ask a model to explain scope and assumptions whenever a delivery estimate changes sharply.
items.body_notes: The creator shares a conversation where a one-month project estimate turned into a one-year estimate after the user asked for a more realistic schedule with proper features. The exchange does not establish the actual project duration.

items.title: An Antigravity Swarm Animates a Pelican
items.takeaway: Assign animation and sound to a coding swarm and inspect the assembled scene.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Carbon and Hydrogen for a JavaScript pelican scene that moves between art styles. The creator says the music and sound are code-generated.

items.title: A Calendar Question with Leap-Year Edge Cases
items.takeaway: Ask a simple conversion question and check whether the answer accounts for calendar edge cases.
items.body_notes: The creator asked Hydrogen High and GPT how many seconds are in a year. Both screenshots give standard- and leap-year results, and Hydrogen also gives an average Gregorian-year calculation.

items.title: TAJ VICE in a Single HTML File
items.takeaway: Prototype an explorable map under a single-file constraint and test its remaining bugs.
items.body_notes: The creator built a GTA-inspired game set in fictional Agra with Hydrogen over a session under 12 hours. They describe pure JavaScript, a single HTML file, no external assets, and remaining gameplay bugs.

items.title: Antigravity Through a Google Cloud Project
items.takeaway: Check agent authentication and project billing when enabling Hydrogen through managed credentials.
items.body_notes: The author documents switching Antigravity from a personal plan to a Google Cloud Agent Platform project using application default credentials. Their model selector includes Hydrogen and the source describes reviewing project charges by SKU.

items.title: Stale Subscription Limits in an Answer
items.takeaway: Verify current plan terms and model names against primary sources when evaluating a research assistant.
items.body_notes: The author shows Hydrogen confusing a similar model name and giving obsolete time-window details for a Qwen plan. This post documents specific apparent reference errors in the captured responses.

items.title: Revising a WebGL Animation's Story
items.takeaway: Ask for a stronger narrative when a technically elaborate first pass lacks a clear progression.
items.body_notes: The creator links the first WebGL version and shows a second version after giving feedback about noise and lack of story. They preferred the revision but still favored their Claude Code comparison.

items.title: Carbon Planning and Hydrogen Mobile Implementation
items.takeaway: Give a planning model the interaction design and an execution model the implementation work.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Carbon for planning a mobile app and Hydrogen for implementing it, including Reanimated physics. They describe smooth motion and share the result in a recording.

items.title: Two Models Code a Mountain Dragon Fight
items.takeaway: Compare how generated animation handles two interacting characters in the same scene.
items.body_notes: The creator shares a code-driven comparison of Qwen-4 Max and Hydrogen on a dragon fight above a mountain temple. The source credits a separate prompt creator.

items.title: A 3D Miniature Island from One Prompt
items.takeaway: Check whether a one-shot scene presents a readable arrangement of landmarks, terrain and water.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Hydrogen with building the displayed miniature island in one prompt. The visual shows an island with buildings and other landmarks.

items.title: A Reproducible Three.js Pelican Prompt
items.takeaway: Test whether the legs, wheels, and steering move together in a cycling animation.
items.body_notes: The creator publishes a complete Japanese Three.js prompt and records the Hydrogen output on a coastal road. They report giving the same prompt to GPT-6.1 Terra earlier; the associated recording shows the Hydrogen run.
items.prompt_text: Three.jsを使って3Dシーンを作成：ペリカンが自転車に乗って海岸沿いの道路を進む。 ペリカンが本当に自転車に乗って、両足でペダルを漕ぎ、翼でハンドルを操り、車輪が漕ぐのに合わせて回転する。動作は自然で滑らか。 シーンは生き生きとして詳細豊かで、自然環境、動的効果、光影、インタラクティブ機能を備える。 あなたの3Dモデリング、アニメーション、ビジュアルデザインの能力を最大限に発揮して、洗練された、すぐに実行可能なウェブ作品を完成させて。

items.title: Hydrogen in a T3 Code Setup
items.takeaway: Try a dedicated coding client and track both rolling and weekly quotas during a realistic session.
items.body_notes: The author reports using a Gemini Pro connection in T3 Code for about half a day with Hydrogen. The screenshots and post record their quota experience and distinguish perceived speed from accuracy in the comparison.

items.title: A Hand-Drawn Public-Service Video
items.takeaway: Use a short public-service message to assess a hand-drawn visual treatment.
items.body_notes: The creator presents a hand-drawn-style public-service clip and attributes it to Gemini 4 Hydrogen. The one-pass result is the creator's account; the post does not identify a separate rendering model or disclose the generation process.

items.title: A Cycling Peacock Across Ten Art Styles
items.takeaway: Use a mixed-model swarm to build visual transitions and synchronize sound in code.
items.body_notes: The creator credits a Carbon and Hydrogen swarm for a cycling peacock animation spanning ten art styles. They report creating the visuals, music and sound effects in code.

items.title: One Cottage Prompt Across Three Surfaces
items.takeaway: Check the output format when moving a visual task between model settings and platforms.
items.body_notes: The creator reports a still output from Hydrogen High in Antigravity, Hydrogen Extra High in AI Studio, and Carbon High in Antigravity. An Arena run labeled Hydrogen produced an animated SVG, but the post does not independently identify that checkpoint.

items.title: Same-Prompt Dashboard Comparison
items.takeaway: Compare interface layout and information hierarchy from a shared frontend prompt.
items.body_notes: The author posts side-by-side web interface screenshots attributed to GPT-6.1 Sol and Hydrogen. The screenshots support a visual comparison. The source leaves implementation, settings, and functional behavior unspecified.

items.title: Recreating the React.gg Website from an Image
items.takeaway: Use a reference image as the starting point and check which details still need revision.
items.body_notes: The creator reports giving Hydrogen a reference image to recreate React.gg in a couple of prompts. The source links their demo and acknowledges that the match is imperfect.

items.title: A Singularity-Themed Interactive Panel
items.takeaway: Prototype a short interactive sequence around a single visual concept.
items.body_notes: The creator shares a Singularity-themed interactive panel attributed to Hydrogen. The recording supplies the output but gives little implementation context.

items.title: Two Models Code a Side-Scroller Animation
items.takeaway: Look at motion continuity and build cost when comparing generated action scenes.
items.body_notes: The creator compares Hydrogen and GPT-6 Astra on an animated side-scrolling scene. They favor the natural movement of Hydrogen’s output and report lower cost, based on these two runs.

items.title: Using Gemini as a Running Coach
items.takeaway: Compare a workout log with the coaching suggestions and adjust goals to your baseline.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Gemini Hydrogen for running coaching and shares a workout screenshot after reporting their longest run in about a year. It is a personal example.

items.title: A Browser Game with On-Chain Scores
items.takeaway: Test a desktop browser game and verify how it records scores separately from gameplay.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Hydrogen with helping build Sheytonak, a Base-linked game with scores recorded on-chain. They report desktop optimization and acknowledge mobile issues and remaining bugs.

items.title: Unrendered Math in a Japanese Answer
items.takeaway: Test rendering as well as correctness when a response contains TeX commands.
items.body_notes: The author shows a Japanese Gemini response displaying raw math notation instead of typeset equations after the move to Hydrogen. The screenshot illustrates one formatting failure in the author's interface.

items.title: A Prompt-to-MIDI Composition App
items.takeaway: Prototype a tool that takes a Japanese brief through MIDI, WAV, and piano-roll views.
items.body_notes: The creator shows an app built with Hydrogen that turns Japanese input into an English music prompt, writes MIDI, renders WAV audio, and generates a piano-roll video. These are functions of the demo app.

items.title: Testing an Instruction to Stay Silent
items.takeaway: Check whether a model can produce no reply when a workflow requires one.
items.body_notes: The author shares a screenshot of a no-reply test and reports different behavior from Carbon and Argon. The post shows one set of trials.

items.title: A Concert Recap on One Page
items.takeaway: Turn event information into a one-page visual recap that readers can scan.
items.body_notes: The author shares a Japanese visual recap of a Batten Girls concert and credits Hydrogen for the summary. The source does not show the complete source materials or prompt.

items.title: Three Models Explain an Electric Motor
items.takeaway: Compare visual clarity and instructional controls with one shared simulation prompt.
items.body_notes: The creator compared Hydrogen with two Qwen models and preferred Hydrogen's 3D motor and physics explanations. The judgments are from a single comparison.
items.prompt_text: create a very realistic animation of how an electric motor works showing everything clearly even the magnetic field, electrons etc. single html file. use any libs via cdn

items.title: Two Model Workflows Animate a Desk Scene
items.takeaway: Check scene details, audio level and the final still hold against the original brief.
items.body_notes: The creator compares Hydrogen and Astra-assisted desk animations made from the same prompt through an API setup. They describe the Gemini result as smoother but say it stayed in motion at the end and had quieter audio. The rendering pipeline is unspecified.

items.title: A Daily Montage from an Avatar
items.takeaway: Use a single reference avatar and four everyday scenes to evaluate short storyboard adaptation.
items.body_notes: The creator supplied an X avatar and scenes for studying, eating, checking a phone, and exercising. They share a roughly ten-second result attributed to Hydrogen without specifying the video rendering backend.

items.title: Hydrogen Plans a ComfyUI Character Clip
items.takeaway: Hold the costume and background constant while varying expressions and action across a video brief.
items.body_notes: The creator credits Hydrogen with planning the clip around a reference design, then identifies the separate ComfyUI MiniMax image-to-video pipeline used to render it. They prepared a new opening frame and a 30-shot prompt for the variation.

items.title: Extending Almance Vale to 100 Modules
items.takeaway: Move an existing app into a coding agent and ask it to preserve style while adding modules.
items.body_notes: The creator moved Almance Vale from the Gemini app to Antigravity. They report using Hydrogen Extra through swarm mode to follow existing code conventions and extend the scene to 100 modules over a few hours.

items.title: A 2D Village with Procedural Sound
items.takeaway: Check whether sandbox sound changes with the events on screen as well as tracking build time.
items.body_notes: The creator compared Qwen 4 Max and Hydrogen at Extra High on a 2D village. They report about 75 minutes and $0.90 for Qwen versus 12 minutes and $1.70 for Hydrogen, and prefer how Hydrogen’s music matches events.

items.title: A Widescreen Visual Treatment for a Song
items.takeaway: Give a song and a framing brief to explore how well motion conveys its energy.
items.body_notes: The creator says they gave Hydrogen XHigh only a song, a 21:9 format, and a request for a sense of speed. The source clip shows a fast-moving roadway treatment and gives no details about how it was rendered.

items.title: Niagara Falls with Seven Hydrogen Subagents
items.takeaway: Give a coordinator separate scene components to distribute among implementation agents.
items.body_notes: The author credits Carbon and seven Hydrogen subagents with building a Niagara Falls experience from one prompt in under an hour. The recording shows water, boats, varied viewpoints, and changing environments.

items.title: Continuity Across Two Period Romance Clips
items.takeaway: Specify the details that should persist when continuing a scene in a second clip.
items.body_notes: The creator attributes a short romantic scene set on an ocean liner to a Gemini workflow using Hydrogen. They publish a two-part brief about maintaining character and costume continuity. The post leaves the underlying video model unspecified.

items.title: A Water Sphere in the Gemini App
items.takeaway: Try a simple optical scene and inspect the relationship between highlights and refraction.
items.body_notes: Google shares a Gemini App visual of a water-like sphere with Hydrogen lettering and attributes the creation to Hydrogen. The source supplies the output without explaining the underlying rendering setup.
